payload.reason: One proposal (practice), selected as the core. Five of its internal seams were redesigned where they contradicted measured facts or each other. No second designer contested it.
payload.selection_rationale:
The practice proposal fixes the one cause that has been measured, and it is shaped the way the code already is.

Evidence for the cause:
- This boot shows the full microsoft/Windows-Containers#646 signature: WCsc 211,022 allocs / 0 frees; 211,070 System handles at GrantedAccess 0x00120089.
- The app's own Scanner.Scan gave +5 WCsc, +5 WCri and +5 System handles on an untouched layer subtree, and 0 on a repeat.
- The repro test fails because Scanner.Run lists Layers\<id>\Files with no path exclusion.

Why a pop-time, root-aware exclusion of %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers:
- It is the only fix with structural evidence. Spike 'layer-store-exclusion' made 0 opens under Layers and tripped 0 tripwires. Its pool verdict is VOID because the layer was already touched this boot.
- It is the only variant the no-go spike leaves standing. That spike ruled out a non-root-aware rule, which skipped 3 of 3 subfolders under a root the user picked; the root-aware variant skipped none.
- It is one predicate and cheap to delete once a fixed wcifs.sys ships.

FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT is declined. Its spike produced 0 valid pairs, so it is unproven, and it would change open semantics for every reparse type, cldflt placeholders included.

PoolWatch.ps1 is taken as the project already decided it. Every spike found it missing and improvised a substitute.

Where the proposal stays honest, and this design keeps that:
- The survey measured the wcifs group at about 290 MB of 8.3 GB on this boot. FMfn 1.17 GB, File 1.0 GB, NtfF 433 MB and Toke 789 MB are unattributed.
- So this design does not claim the reported 30 GB is explained. The protocol measures the rest.
- Criterion 5 and the cold per-file question get a conditional second boot, because the single-boot ordering can only compare warm repeats.

Pre-existing and not touched by this design: 3 tests fail in the full suite on this PC (LastAccessTests.cs:87, HeldOpenTreeTests.cs:68/:96; DisableLastAccess=2). They pre-date SL-095 and must not be read as regressions from it. They also touch the SC-070/074 lead, which is one more reason the narrowing step stays conditional and in scratch.

components.name: ContainerLayerStore rule
components.responsibility: Resolves the live layer store once per scan as Environment.GetFolderPath(CommonApplicationData) + \Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers. It strips any \\?\ prefix, normalises with GetFullPath and trims any trailing separator. It answers two pure questions. IsActiveFor(scanRoot) is false when the normalised root is at or under the store. IsInside(folderPath) uses OrdinalIgnoreCase with a separator boundary, so 'Layers2' does not match. If the known folder cannot be resolved (empty string), the entry is dropped before any compare: an empty prefix must never match every path. No I/O and no handle to the store. This is the only file in src that composes the store path.
components.key_interactions: ScanOptions holds its result as the default excluded-store list. Scanner calls IsActiveFor once per scan and IsInside once per popped folder.

components.name: ScanOptions excluded-store list
components.responsibility: Carries the excluded stores. The default is [ContainerLayerStore location], so the App and the SL-095 bug test get the rule without opting in. Tests replace the list with a folder under %TEMP%. An empty list turns the rule off. There is no user setting.
components.key_interactions: Sits beside the existing AfterFolder seam that the bug test uses.

components.name: Scanner descent check
components.responsibility: In Run.Execute, right after _pending.Pop() and before DirectoryReader.Read or any SynchronousIoCancel.OpenDirectory, a folder the active rule says is inside a store is completed without being opened. It goes through the SAME completion path an access-denied folder takes: 0 children, a not-read record, parent roll-up proceeds, and progress advances. It does not call AfterFolder, because the folder was never listed. Full and cancelled scans share the loop, so both are covered.
components.key_interactions: FolderDone still pushes every Folder-kind child unchanged. EntryClassifier.cs:10 and EntryKind.cs:6 are untouched, so WCI folders outside the store are still entered as intended. DirectoryReader.cs and the open path are not changed.

components.name: Skipped-store record
components.responsibility: The existing record of folders the scan did not read gains a distinct reason, 'skipped on purpose: container layer store'. It is not a Win32 access failure and is not counted as unreadable-by-error. The change is additive to the not-read record and to the schema-1 --report output: add a reason field if only a Win32 code is serialised today, and never reuse an error code as a sentinel.
components.lives_at: src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/Scanner.cs (existing not-read record) and the schema-1 report writer
components.key_interactions: Read by the App's unreadable-folders panel and by eng/read-window.ps1.

components.name: Unreadable-folders panel row
components.responsibility: Shows the skipped store as 'Not scanned: Windows container layer store. Walking it makes wcifs.sys leak kernel memory until restart.' The path comes from the record and is never hard-coded in App code. 'Open in Explorer' behaves as it does for any row.
components.key_interactions: Renders only what the Core record carries.

components.name: ContainerLayerStore / scanner tests on real temp trees
components.responsibility: xUnit tests on %TEMP% NTFS trees with an injected fake store. They cover every material case below: root above, at and under the store; \\?\ prefix, case and trailing-separator forms; the sibling prefix; no store present; empty or unresolvable entry; the skipped folder being the last pending child; and a scan cancelled while the store is pending. An open-counting hook asserts 0 opens under the fake store. The existing counting-rule tests run unchanged.
components.key_interactions: Uses the ScanOptions store list and the AfterFolder seam.

components.name: SL-095 bug test (acceptance)
components.responsibility: Commit the untracked repro project unchanged. `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/bugs/SL-095-ContainerLayerWalk/SL-095-ContainerLayerWalk.Tests.csproj` must exit 0: a scan rooted at C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Containers lists no folder of Layers\<id>\Files.
components.key_interactions: Relies on the rule being on by default in ScanOptions. Its assembly name is FsAnalyser.Core.Tests, the same as the real Core.Tests. Build decides whether it joins FsAnalyser.slnx, and must keep the outputs apart.

components.name: PoolWatch.ps1 (mark / diff)
components.responsibility:
The tool the project already decided on. Runs unelevated under PS 5.1 and pwsh 7.
- -Mark writes one JSONL line: timestamp, label, arm, run number, boot time, uptime, and whether FsAnalyser.exe is running.
- It also records GetPerformanceInfo paged/nonpaged totals and the System (PID 4) handles, in total and at GrantedAccess 0x00120089 (SystemExtendedHandleInformation, class 64).
- All pool tags go in as an array (SystemPoolTagInformation, class 22). Buffers are sized from the length each call returns and retried on STATUS_INFO_LENGTH_MISMATCH.
- A session-start env record adds: OS build, wcifs.sys version, HiberbootEnabled, DisableLastAccess, SecurityCenter2 AV products, OneDrive/CmService running, and the state of wcifs, bindflt, CldFlt and WdFilter.
- -Diff prints drift-corrected per-pool and per-tag deltas, then PASS/FAIL against the stated tolerance.
components.key_interactions: Seeded from the spikes' scratch pw/PoolMark.ps1 and the repro's .taad-scratch/tagdelta.ps1. Logs are committed under docs/design/SL-095-runs/.

components.name: Protocol mode (person-run, Boot A and conditional Boot B)
components.responsibility:
Boot A starts straight after a true Restart; it refuses if uptime is over 15 min or FsAnalyser.exe is running. Order:
1. Idle for at least 10 min.
2. 5 completed C: scans.
3. 5 cancelled scans: 3 with Cancel, 2 with the window closed.
4. Idle for at least 10 min.
5. Positive control: `cmd /c dir /a /s /b <Layers> > NUL`.
6. `cmd /c dir /a /s /b C:\ > NUL`, twice.
Each app run is marked before, when done or cancelled, and 60 s after exit. The session is VOID if the positive control leaks 0 WCsc.

Boot B runs only if Boot A's app runs break the tolerance on FMfn/File/NtfF. After a true Restart:
1. Idle.
2. A scratch build with the per-file metadata probe off (listing only, Layers still excluded), twice, while file paths are cold.
3. The shipped app, twice.
4. Idle.
The first shipped run's delta over the listing-only runs is what per-file opens cost.

Every step waits on the process or on the person, never on a fixed sleep.
components.key_interactions: Launches the published exe with --report <file> so each run records how far it got. Does not use FsaWindowHook. Whole-drive scans, the restarts and the elevated `fltmc filters` / `fltmc instances` output come from the person.

components.name: Findings and workaround record
components.key_interactions: Validate fills the tables from the committed JSONL.

contracts.name: ContainerLayerStore.IsActiveFor(scanRoot) / IsInside(folderPath)
contracts.notes: Both inputs are normalised the same way: strip \\?\, GetFullPath, trim any trailing separator, OrdinalIgnoreCase, separator-bounded at-or-under. The rule is active only when the root is outside every store. It costs one string compare per popped folder.
contracts.error_cases: If the known folder is unresolvable or empty, the entry is dropped, no store is excluded, and the scan behaves as before. It never throws into the scan, and an empty prefix never reaches the compare.

contracts.name: ScanOptions excluded-store list
contracts.notes: The default is [ContainerLayerStore location]. Tests inject a temp path, and an empty list disables the rule. There is no App UI for it.
contracts.error_cases: Relative, empty or unnormalisable entries are ignored.

contracts.name: Not-read folder record: reason 'skipped: container layer store'
contracts.notes: Kept apart from access failures and additive to the record and the schema-1 --report, with no schema version bump. A reason field is added if the report carries only a Win32 code; an error code is never reused as a sentinel.
contracts.error_cases: Scans that never reach a store produce no such record, so read-window assertions that count unreadable folders are unchanged for them.

contracts.name: Unreadable-folders panel row
contracts.notes: 'Not scanned: Windows container layer store (<path from record>). Walking it makes wcifs.sys leak kernel memory until restart.' Open in Explorer works as for any row.

contracts.name: PoolWatch.ps1 -Mark -Label <s> [-Arm completed|cancelled|control|listing|idle] [-Run n] -Out <jsonl>
contracts.auth_model: Ordinary user only. No elevation, poolmon, WDK or ETW.
contracts.notes: One JSON object per line. Tags are an array of {tag, pagedAllocs, pagedFrees, pagedBytes, npAllocs, npFrees, npBytes}. The line also holds PID 4 handles, in total and at 0x00120089. A mark takes about 0.25 s.
contracts.error_cases: STATUS_INFO_LENGTH_MISMATCH: grow the buffer and retry. If the handle query fails, the handle fields are null and the mark is still written.

contracts.name: PoolWatch.ps1 -Diff -From <label> -To <label> [-DriftFrom <label> -DriftTo <label>] -In <jsonl>
contracts.notes: Per-pool and per-tag deltas, corrected by idle-drift rate × elapsed time, then a PASS/FAIL line against the tolerance in key_decisions.

contracts.name: PoolWatch.ps1 -Protocol -Boot A|B -Exe <published FsAnalyser.exe> -Out docs/design/SL-095-runs/
contracts.auth_model: Unelevated. The person restarts, approves and starts each whole-drive scan, and pastes the elevated fltmc output separately.
contracts.notes: Writes one JSONL per arm plus the env record. Boot B needs -ListingOnlyExe <scratch build with the per-file probe off>, built from `git archive` and never shipped.
contracts.error_cases: Refuses if uptime is over 15 min or FsAnalyser.exe is running. If the Boot A positive control leaks 0 WCsc, the session is marked VOID: the fixed runs prove nothing on an already-touched boot.

key_decisions.decision: The fix is a root-aware descent exclusion of %ProgramData%\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers. It is checked right after a folder is popped and before any open, and it is inactive when the scan root is at or under the store.
key_decisions.rationale: It addresses the only proven cause, the wcifs.sys first-touch leak (#646), which the app's own scanner triggered (+5/+5/+5). Evidence: the exclusion spike made 0 opens under Layers; the no-go spike forbids a non-root-aware rule, and its root-aware variant skipped none. It is one predicate, deleted when Microsoft ships a fixed wcifs.sys.

key_decisions.decision: Exclude the whole Layers store: not all of Containers, and not only Layers\<id>\Files.
key_decisions.rationale: Excluding Containers would turn a root-aware rule off for the acceptance test's own root (Containers), so the test would still fail. Whole-Layers is the scope the spike validated at 0 opens. The narrower Files-only rule would open Layers\<id>, Hives, Bindings and Specialization, which nobody has measured. The cost is that those folders' real bytes go uncounted, shown as a not-scanned row; that trade is an open question for the person.

key_decisions.decision: Match the store by its location, resolved from the CommonApplicationData known folder, not by reparse tag or file ID.
key_decisions.rationale: A live layer hides its WCI tags: its Files\Windows directories carry no ReparsePoint or Offline attributes, so a tag test cannot see it. A file-ID match needs an open of the store. Junctions are not followed, so descent from the parent is the only way in.

key_decisions.decision: Do not add FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT to the scanner's opens.
key_decisions.rationale: The ORP spike produced 0 valid pairs. It would change open semantics for every reparse type, including cldflt placeholders (SC-063) and the counting-rule paths, only to protect a root picked inside the store, and that case is a person's decision (open question).

key_decisions.decision: A skipped store is completed through the existing access-denied completion path, with a distinct reason, and shown in the panel. The panel renders the path from the record.
key_decisions.rationale: A popped folder that is neither listed nor completed stalls its parent's roll-up and progress. The record feeds the UI panel and the schema-1 --report read by eng/read-window.ps1, so it is a contract with more than one consumer and is kept additive. One owner of the path means no second, non-root-aware check can creep in.

key_decisions.decision: The rule is on by default through ScanOptions, with the store list injectable. No user setting.
key_decisions.rationale: The App and the bug test both use defaults. Injection lets temp-tree tests exercise the rule without the real store, and a later Docker windowsfilter entry is one line of data.

key_decisions.decision: Build tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1 exactly as the project decided: unelevated class-22 tags, GetPerformanceInfo totals, JSONL with a tags array, committed under docs/design/SL-095-runs/. Add the PID 4 handle count at 0x00120089 and an env record.
key_decisions.rationale: The tool was decided but is missing, and every spike improvised a replacement. The PID 4 0x00120089 count (211,070, against 211,022 live WCsc) is the leak's cleanest per-object signature.

key_decisions.decision: Validation runs in Boot A: a true Restart, then idle, 5 completed, 5 cancelled, idle, positive control, and `dir /s` of C: twice. Boot B follows only if Boot A breaks the tolerance: a listing-only scratch build first, then the shipped app.
key_decisions.rationale: First touch is single-use per boot. Running the fixed app first and the leaking control last makes the fixed runs VALID exactly when the control then leaks about 210K WCsc. In Boot A the `dir /s` runs come after the app, so they only compare warm repeats (criterion 5, scan-after-scan). Attributing the cold FMfn/File/NtfF mass to per-file opens needs its own fresh boot, with the listing-only arm first.

256 MiB is under 1% of 31 GB, and it catches the reported build-up. 32 MiB catches the 'grows every scan' shape. Drift correction absorbs the CmService zygote's own wcifs leak and the ambient 25H2 growth. If a cold first scan alone breaks 256 MiB, the row says FAIL and the slice routes to the decidable disagreement. The tolerance is not widened to make it pass.

key_decisions.decision: Narrowing is conditional and done in scratch builds from `git archive`, one behaviour off at a time (SC-070/074, SC-067, SC-017, SC-011). No toggles ship. If SC-011, the per-file probe, is implicated, it goes to the person.
key_decisions.rationale: Shipped diagnostic toggles would be platform work for a one-time question. The per-file probe is SL-056's rule, which the person decided in Q-004, so changing it is the person's call, not a side-effect of this design.

proposals.note: The only proposal. Its fix, measurement tool, protocol, tolerance and escalation path are taken. Changes made: the skip is routed through the existing not-read completion path; an empty known-folder prefix can no longer match everything; the panel renders the record's path instead of hard-coding it; a conditional Boot B was added for cold per-file attribution; and a root picked inside the store is raised to the person rather than accepted silently.

payload.coherence_check:
There was one proposal (practice), so there is no composition to check. Nothing in this design has survived a disagreement, and the reviewer is the first to argue with it.

Instead, the proposal was checked for internal contradictions and against what was measured. Five seams were changed:

(1) Pop-time skip vs parent completion. 'Skip the folder' left a popped folder neither listed nor completed, which stalls the parent's roll-up and progress. Redesigned: the skip goes through the same completion path an access-denied folder takes (0 children, a not-read record, no AfterFolder call). The only difference is that no open is issued.

(2) Panel text vs one owner of the path. The proposal's UI string hard-coded C:\ProgramData\...\Containers\Layers, which would let a second copy of the path, and later a second non-root-aware check, grow outside the predicate. Redesigned: the panel renders the record's path, and ContainerLayerStore.cs is the only file in src that composes it (architecture rule 1).

(3) Unresolvable known folder. The proposal said 'no store is excluded', but an empty prefix in an at-or-under test matches every path and would skip the whole scan. Redesigned: empty or unresolvable entries are dropped before any compare, and this is listed as a material case.

(4) Single-boot ordering vs criterion 5 and the unattributed mass. In one boot, `dir /s` runs after the app on warm paths, so it only compares repeat-scan growth. It cannot say whether the cold per-file open is what retains FMfn/File/NtfF (the survey: wcifs is about 290 MB of 8.3 GB). Added a conditional Boot B with a listing-only arm first.

(5) Root-aware rule without ORP. Together they leave a root the user picks inside the store still leaking. Kept, because the no-go spike forbids a non-root-aware rule and ORP has 0 valid pairs, but raised as an open question instead of being accepted silently.

Checks that held:
- The root-aware exclusion of Layers, not Containers, is active for the acceptance test's root (Containers), so the test passes.
- Declining ORP leaves the SC-063 cldflt open semantics unchanged.
- The strict tolerance with no cold-fill exemption is consistent with the 25H2 FMfn retention evidence. If it fails, the slice routes to the decidable disagreement, not to a wider tolerance.

Nobody has contested the idea that wcifs is the app's whole contribution to the reported 30 GB. This design fixes the proven cause and measures the rest rather than assuming it.

architecture_rules.name: only ContainerLayerStore composes the container layer store path
architecture_rules.because: A second hand-written check of the store path reproduces the no-go the spike measured: a rule that is not root-aware skipped 3 of 3 subfolders when the user picked a root inside the store. A copy that skips the \\?\ strip or the separator boundary either walks the live layer again, leaking wcifs pool until a restart, or excludes a sibling folder the user wants counted.

architecture_rules.name: the pool measurement never needs elevation
architecture_rules.because: The protocol runs once per fresh boot, and first touch of the layer is single-use. An elevation prompt, or a tool that fails unelevated, spoils a boot the person had to restart for. The project decided on unelevated SystemPoolTagInformation marks, with fltmc output supplied separately by the person.

cases.behaviour: scan a folder above the container store
cases.shape: root is C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Containers (or C:\) and a live layer sits under Layers
cases.why: This is the acceptance test. The pop-time predicate must fire before DirectoryReader.Read opens Layers. Any open beneath it makes wcifs resolve WCI reparse points and leak WCsc/WCfc/WCri plus a System handle until a restart.

cases.behaviour: scan a folder the user picked
cases.shape: the root is the store itself (…\Containers\Layers)
cases.why: This is the no-go spike's measured failure: a rule that is not root-aware skipped every subfolder of a root the user picked. IsActiveFor must return false here.

cases.behaviour: scan a folder the user picked
cases.shape: the root is deep under the store (Layers\<id>\Files\Windows\System32\Speech)
cases.why: The at-or-under test on the root must also turn the rule off for deeper roots, or the scan reports 3 empty folders, which is what the spike saw.

cases.shape: the popped folder path carries a \\?\ prefix, different case, or a trailing separator
cases.why: The scanner uses long-path forms (a counting rule). A raw compare misses them and the store gets walked.
Without a separator boundary the prefix test excludes a folder the user wants counted, and the under-count is silent.

cases.shape: there is no container store on the machine at all
cases.why: Most PCs look like this. There must be no skip record, no extra panel row, and unchanged unreadable counts in --report.

cases.shape: the known folder resolves to an empty string, or the store list is empty
cases.why: GetFolderPath returns "" on failure, and an empty prefix in an at-or-under compare matches every path and skips the entire scan.

cases.shape: the skipped store folder is the last pending child of its parent
cases.why: The skip issues no open, so it must take the access-denied completion path. Otherwise the parent's roll-up never finishes, progress stalls, or AfterFolder fires for a folder that was never listed.

cases.shape: the scan is cancelled (Cancel, or the window closed) while the store folder is still pending
cases.why: This is DONE (c)'s cancelled arm. The skip must not interact with the SC-017 CancelSynchronousIo path, and no open under Layers may be issued on the way out.

cases.shape: the result holds both an access-denied folder and the skipped store
cases.why: The schema-1 --report and the panel must tell them apart. Encoding the skip as a Win32 code sentinel would change read-window unreadable counts on every C: scan.

cases.shape: the boot has already walked the layer (uptime over 15 min, or the positive control leaks 0 WCsc)
cases.why: First touch is single-use per boot. Fixed runs on a touched boot pass vacuously, which is exactly what voided the ORP and exclusion spikes.

cases.shape: the tag or handle table grows between the size query and the read (STATUS_INFO_LENGTH_MISMATCH)
cases.why: Without a retry a mark is lost on a boot that cannot be repeated.

cases.shape: a Docker windowsfilter layer store (C:\ProgramData\docker\windowsfilter\<id>\Files) is present
cases.why: Not present on this PC and not measured. The store list is data, so adding it later is one entry. Recorded so the next slice can disagree.

cases.shape: the path is in 8.3 short form, is reached through a junction, or is on another drive
cases.why: Child paths are built from the long names in the listing, junctions are not followed, and OpenFolderDialog returns long names. Another drive can never be at or under a C: prefix.

decidable_disagreements.question: Does the unattributed FMfn/File/NtfF mass come from the app's per-file metadata open (the SL-056 probe)? That is: does a scan with the fix in place still break the tolerance on a cold C: scan while a listing-only walk of the same paths does not? On this boot that mass is 1.17 GB / 1.0 GB / 433 MB outstanding, against about 290 MB of wcifs.
decidable_disagreements.positions:
The proposal and the investigation treat the wcifs first-touch leak as the app's cause. They ruled out the app's own handles: File was about +4 per run whatever the tree size, on small, probably warm trees.

On the other side:
- The survey measured wcifs at about 290 MB of 8.3 GB.
- The repeat-walk marks still grew FMfn by about 3.6K net per five walks.
- Microsoft Q&A 5966064 reports 25H2 keeping about 1 KB of FMfn/File per first-time open.

Outcomes:
- Boot A within tolerance: the exclusion is the whole fix.
- Boot B shows the listing-only arm within tolerance but the per-file probe arm not: the SizeProbe from SL-056 (Q-004, the person's decision) is implicated. The component boundary and the counting contract change, which needs re-synthesis and the person.
- Both arms fail alike: the cause is the OS. DONE (b) becomes a documented workaround (true Restart), and the tolerance row records FAIL.

taste_disagreements: Uncontested so far: the skipped store goes into the existing unreadable-folders panel with its own reason, rather than into a separate 'skipped on purpose' list.

Uncontested so far: the whole Layers store is excluded (the scope the spike validated) rather than only Layers\<id>\Files (keeps Hives/Bindings bytes counted, but nobody has measured whether those folders leak). Partly empirical: Boot A's positive control could be extended to list the non-Files children.
Uncontested so far: ScanOptions carries a general excluded-store list rather than a single dedicated bool. The list was chosen for test injection and for a later Docker windowsfilter entry.
open_questions: When the person deliberately picks a scan root at or inside C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Containers\Layers, should the app scan it as picked (this design: yes, and wcifs.sys leaks pool and a System handle for each untouched entry until a true Restart), warn before scanning, or refuse? FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT might make scanning safe, but it has 0 valid measurements.

Excluding the whole Layers store leaves its real bytes out of C: totals, shown only as a not-scanned row: Hives, Bindings, Specialization and dotnet.bcf, whose size has not been measured. Is that acceptable under the counting rule, or should the exclusion narrow to Layers\<id>\Files once a fresh-boot measurement shows the non-Files children do not leak?
channeled_experts: Windows minifilter / Filter Manager engineer (wcifs, FltMgr context lifetimes)
Sysinternals-style kernel pool and handle leak triage
Measurement discipline for single-use state: drift-corrected A/B with an ordered positive control

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Antivirus and backup file crawlers running on Windows container hosts
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Leave the virtualised layer store out of the walk, identified by where it lives rather than by per-entry attributes, because its contents are projections of host files already covered elsewhere. Still honour an explicit target the user points inside it.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: FsAnalyser is a crawler with the same exposure: it walks everything readable under C:, including a store whose Files entries are placeholders of host files. The location-based exclusion transfers directly. The 'honour an explicit target' half transfers structurally, since the root-aware rule skips nothing, but not safely: here an explicit walk leaks.

invariants.precondition: The layer store can be identified by location without opening it.
invariants.evidence: The investigation found the live layer's Files\Windows directories carry no ReparsePoint or Offline attributes, so a tag test cannot see them. The exclusion spike's path predicate gave 0 opens under Layers, with 0 tripwires across CreateFile, OpenDirectory and SizeProbe.

invariants.precondition: Everything in the store is a projection of host files counted elsewhere, so skipping it loses no bytes.
invariants.evidence: The Files entries are placeholders (CloudOnly, not local bytes). Layers\<id> also holds Hives, Bindings, Specialization and dotnet.bcf, whose bytes are real, are not measured, and go uncounted under a whole-Layers exclusion.

invariants.precondition: An explicit target the user picks inside the store can be walked without harm.
invariants.evidence: #646 and this boot's scanner probe show that any walk of untouched layer entries leaks. The root-aware variant skipped none of the opens in the no-go spike's case (b), but ORP produced 0 valid leak pairs, so an honoured target still leaks. Raised to the person.

prior_art.pattern: Find a kernel leak by pool tag: sort tags by bytes, then diff allocs against frees across a workload. This is the same data PoolWatch reads unelevated through SystemPoolTagInformation.
Map pool tags to owning drivers through pooltag.txt, for naming the FMfn (FltMgr), File, NtfF (NTFS) and Toke owners in the findings record.

Windows 11 25H2 retains FMfn/FMsc/FMsl/File/IoFE/IoNm/NtfF/NtFC after cold file-name operations, about 1 KB per first-time path; 24.4 GB in 47 h; a reboot clears it. This is the basis for the listing-only vs per-file-open comparison.
Attribute the owning driver with WPA pool-allocation stacks when poolmon gives only a tag. Rejected here: the project decided no ETW, no WPR/WPA and no elevation.

wcifs.sys leaks WCsc/WCfc/WCri/FMwi/FMfc plus one System handle on the first touch of each WCI entry in a live layer. Any walker triggers it, including dir /s. The mitigation is to avoid walking the layer store, and a true restart reclaims the memory.
prior_art.where: microsoft/Windows-Containers issue #646 (and microsoft/WSL #41296 'fixinbound'), as recorded by the investigation stage

prior_art.pattern: Antivirus and backup crawlers on container hosts exclude or short-circuit container layer stores, because they are projections of host files already scanned directly.
prior_art.where: Microsoft guidance on antivirus optimisation for Windows containers
